    LargeIndecomposable.IndSkeleton.arTranslationQuiver

    The Auslander--Reiten quiver as a translation quiver #

    the vertices of Γ_A are the indecomposable modules, and the arrows X → Y form a basis of Irr(X, Y) = J(X, Y)/J²(X, Y). The translation τ sends a nonprojective indecomposable Y to the starting term of the almost split sequence ending at Y; it is a bijection from the nonprojective onto the noninjective vertices. The mates of the arrows ending at a nonprojective Y are the arrows starting at τY, indexed by the same summands of the middle term.

    Formally the arrows X → Y are Fin (dim Irr(X, Y)); the mate bijection (y ⟶ x) ≃ (τx ⟶ y) is the identification of these index sets, which have the same size because both dimensions equal the multiplicity of y in the middle term of the almost split sequence ending at x. The projective and injective vertices are those whose module is projective, respectively injective, in mod A. The translation and the dimension identities come from the Auslander--Reiten theory through ARBridge.lean.
